overall_summary: The channel's clear growth driver is extreme space anomalies and exoplanets with bizarre physical properties (e.g., TrES-2b, burning ice, ruby rain). These cosmic mystery topics consistently outperform generic animal facts, psychology tricks, and brain facts, driving the highest views and engagement. Additionally, slightly longer Shorts (16-21 seconds) perform significantly better than ultra-short 12-15 second clips.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,018 views, 36 likes), 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views, 8 likes), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views, 25 likes) are the top-performing videos.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space science, focusing on planets with mind-bending weather, composition, or physical laws.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views) and 'The Largest Ocean in Space' (460 views) show strong baseline interest in sensory-based cosmic facts.
winning_patterns.action: Frame space topics around human senses or familiar concepts scaled to cosmic proportions.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (multiple uploads, maxing out at 53 views) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) consistently underperform.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic cognitive psychology facts unless they can be tied to a highly cinematic, historical, or mysterious narrative.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (183 views) and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views) fail to capture the high-velocity curiosity of the space-themed content.
weak_patterns.action: Limit standard animal trivia; if covering animals, pivot to cinematic survival stories or ancient/prehistoric beasts.

next_video.opening_direction: There is a planet twice the size of Earth made entirely of solid diamond.
next_video.twist_direction: But don't pack your bags yet—the surface temperature is a crushing 3,900 degrees, turning the diamond into a pressurized liquid nightmare.
next_video.reason: Exoplanets with extreme, high-contrast conditions (like burning ice or ruby rain) are our top performers. A 21-second duration matches the exact length of our most successful uploads, allowing enough time to build tension and deliver a satisfying twist.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' space survival scenario (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into a Planet of Liquid Metal?') to merge the high-performing exoplanet category with cinematic storytelling.
